newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin asks France's Socialists for loyal support.
newsitem.headline: Jospin asks France's Socialists for loyal support.

text.p: Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, in power barely a month, asked members of his Socialist Party on Saturday to "respect the rules of the game" and loyally support his agenda for France.
In a speech to a party congress in Paris, Jospin pledged to pay attention to their advice on national policy and, in return, they could share in the leftist government's successes.
"Our success will be collective," Jospin told the closed-door meeting, according to spokesman Manuel Valls.
"Nothing will be done without your advice. The Socialists will be closely involved in all decisions," Valls quoted him as saying. "There will be no grumpy spectators."
The leftist government combining Socialists, Communists and Greens was swept into power in a June 1 parliamentary election upset.
Barely a month later, it has already begun running into criticism from trade unions, family associations and opposition politicians over some of its early moves.

Jospin has also been accused of moving too slowly on key economic policy matters after delaying decisions until autumn on campaign promises to create 700,000 new jobs, cut the working week to 35 hours from 39 without a cut in pay and meet the requirements for adoption of the single European currency.
Jospin also was clearly irritated by criticism from leftist allies, including Socialist members of parliament, over his handling of the closing of a Renault car assembly plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium.
Jospin has insisted he kept a campaign promise to review Renault's decision though the plant will still close.
As a result of his review, some of the plant's workers will be redeployed and none will be paid off outright, he boasted earlier this week.
The French state owns 46 percent of Renault's shares.
